claim: The retinoblastoma Rb protein is an important factor controlling the cell cycle.
source: The retinoblastoma Rb protein is an important factor controlling the cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background knowledge about Rb function.

claim: Mammalian cells carrying Rb deletions are still able to arrest under growth-limiting conditions.
source: Yet, mammalian cells carrying Rb deletions are still able to arrest under growth-limiting conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Hurford et al., 1997; Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000; Herrera et al., 1996).

claim: p130 and p107 are not sufficient for DREAM-dependent repression.
source: Here, we show that p130 and p107 are not sufficient for DREAM-dependent repression.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing DREAM loses function without Lin37 even when p130/p107 are present.

claim: Lin37 is an essential factor for DREAM function.
source: We identify the MuvB protein Lin37 as an essential factor for DREAM function.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments showing loss of DREAM repression in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: Cells not expressing Lin37 proliferate normally.
source: Cells not expressing Lin37 proliferate normally, but DREAM completely loses its ability to repress genes in G0/G1 while all remaining subunits, including p130/p107, still bind to target gene promoters.
evidence: This is supported by MTT assays (Figure 2B) and cell cycle analysis showing Lin37 knockout cells can proliferate.

claim: DREAM completely loses its ability to repress genes in G0/G1 in cells not expressing Lin37.
source: Cells not expressing Lin37 proliferate normally, but DREAM completely loses its ability to repress genes in G0/G1 while all remaining subunits, including p130/p107, still bind to target gene promoters.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data (Figure 3B), luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4), and RNA-seq data (Figure 6).

claim: All remaining DREAM subunits, including p130/p107, still bind to target gene promoters in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: Cells not expressing Lin37 proliferate normally, but DREAM completely loses its ability to repress genes in G0/G1 while all remaining subunits, including p130/p107, still bind to target gene promoters.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP experiments (Figure 7B) and DNA pulldown assays (Figure 7A).

claim: Cells lacking both Rb and Lin37 are incapable of exiting the cell cycle.
source: Furthermore, cells lacking both Rb and Lin37 are incapable of exiting the cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9B) and gene expression data (Figure 9C, D) showing Lin37/Rb double knockout cells cannot arrest.

claim: Lin37 cooperates with Rb to induce quiescence.
source: Thus, Lin37 is an essential component of DREAM that cooperates with Rb to induce quiescence.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by the double knockout experiments showing loss of cell cycle arrest when both are absent.

claim: Rb is mutated in many cancer types.
source: The retinoblastoma protein Rb regulates cell cycle-dependent gene expression and is mutated in many cancer types (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hanahan and Weinberg, 2000.

claim: Rb and the related proteins p130 and p107 are members of the pocket protein family.
source: Rb and the related proteins p130 and p107 are members of the pocket protein family.
evidence: This is established knowledge about protein family classification.

claim: Pocket proteins interact with E2f proteins to form complexes that repress expression of genes necessary for cell cycle progression in G0 and early G1.
source: All of them interact with E2f proteins to form complexes that repress expression of genes necessary for cell cycle progression in G0 and early G1 (Classon and Dyson, 2001; Classon and Harlow, 2002; Cobrinik, 2005; Dick and Rubin, 2013; Burkhart and Sage, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing pocket protein function.

claim: Rb preferentially interacts with E2f1-3.
source: Rb preferentially interacts with E2f1-3, and p130/p107 mainly bind to E2f4/5 (Helin et al., 1992; Lees et al., 1993; Liban et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Helin et al., 1992; Lees et al., 1993; Liban et al., 2017.

claim: p130/p107 mainly bind to E2f4/5.
source: Rb preferentially interacts with E2f1-3, and p130/p107 mainly bind to E2f4/5 (Helin et al., 1992; Lees et al., 1993; Liban et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Helin et al., 1992; Lees et al., 1993; Liban et al., 2017.

claim: p107 or p130 are components of the DREAM complex.
source: p107 or p130 are components of the DREAM complex (Guiley et al., 2015; Litovchick et al., 2007; Pilkinton et al., 2007; Schmit et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing DREAM complex composition.

claim: DREAM binds and represses cell cycle genes with maximal expression in S, G2, and M phases through E2F and CHR promoter elements.
source: While DREAM binds and represses cell cycle genes with maximal expression in S, G2, and M phases through E2F and CHR promoter elements, E2f-Rb complexes cannot bind to CHR sites.
evidence: This is supported by citations (Litovchick et al., 2007; Hurford et al., 1997; Müller et al., 2014; Müller et al., 2016).

claim: E2f-Rb complexes cannot bind to CHR sites.
source: While DREAM binds and represses cell cycle genes with maximal expression in S, G2, and M phases through E2F and CHR promoter elements, E2f-Rb complexes cannot bind to CHR sites.
evidence: This is supported by citations (Litovchick et al., 2007; Hurford et al., 1997; Müller et al., 2014; Müller et al., 2016).

claim: E2f-Rb complexes can interact with E2F binding sites of S phase genes.
source: However, they can interact with E2F binding sites of S phase genes (Litovchick et al., 2007; Hurford et al., 1997; Müller et al., 2014; Müller et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing E2f-Rb binding specificity.

claim: Rb and p130/p107 have overlapping, but also clearly distinct functions in the repression of cell cycle genes.
source: Thus, Rb and p130/p107 have overlapping, but also clearly distinct functions in the repression of cell cycle genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the different binding specificities and complex compositions described.

claim: Pocket protein triple knockout cells can proliferate.
source: Pocket protein triple knockout cells can proliferate, but are unable to exit the cell cycle under growth-limiting conditions (Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000.

claim: Pocket protein triple knockout cells are unable to exit the cell cycle under growth-limiting conditions.
source: Pocket protein triple knockout cells can proliferate, but are unable to exit the cell cycle under growth-limiting conditions (Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000.

claim: Rb−/− cells largely maintain their potential to arrest in G0.
source: In contrast, Rb−/− or p130−/−/p107−/− cells largely maintain their potential to arrest in G0 (Hurford et al., 1997; Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000; Herrera et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: p130−/−/p107−/− cells largely maintain their potential to arrest in G0.
source: In contrast, Rb−/− or p130−/−/p107−/− cells largely maintain their potential to arrest in G0 (Hurford et al., 1997; Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000; Herrera et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The MuvB core complex consists of Lin54, Lin52, Lin37, Lin9, and Rbbp4.
source: The MuvB core complex consists of Lin54, Lin52, Lin37, Lin9, and Rbbp4.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MuvB complex composition.

claim: The p130/p107-E2f4/5-Dp module is recruited to the MuvB core through a direct interaction of p130/p107 with Lin52 phosphorylated at Serine 28.
source: The p130/p107-E2f4/5-Dp module is recruited to the MuvB core through a direct interaction of p130/p107 with Lin52 phosphorylated at Serine 28 (Guiley et al., 2015; Litovchick et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Guiley et al., 2015; Litovchick et al., 2011.

claim: Lin54 mediates binding of MuvB complexes to DNA through CHR promoter elements of G2/M cell cycle genes.
source: Lin54 mediates binding of MuvB complexes to DNA through CHR promoter elements of G2/M cell cycle genes (Marceau et al., 2016; Schmit et al., 2009), and E2f4/5-Dp interact with E2F sites in promoters of G1/S genes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Marceau et al., 2016; Schmit et al., 2009.

claim: E2f4/5-Dp interact with E2F sites in promoters of G1/S genes.
source: Lin54 mediates binding of MuvB complexes to DNA through CHR promoter elements of G2/M cell cycle genes (Marceau et al., 2016; Schmit et al., 2009), and E2f4/5-Dp interact with E2F sites in promoters of G1/S genes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about E2f4/5-Dp binding specificity.

claim: DREAM is recruited to a broad set of cell cycle genes because of its binding to E2F and CHR sites.
source: Because of its binding to E2F and CHR sites, DREAM is recruited to a broad set of cell cycle genes (Litovchick et al., 2007; Müller et al., 2014; Müller et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing DREAM target genes.

claim: Lin9 binds to several MuvB complex proteins.
source: Since Lin9 binds to several MuvB complex proteins (Schmit et al., 2007; Wiseman et al., 2015), it seems to be the central structural component of MuvB complexes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schmit et al., 2007; Wiseman et al., 2015.

claim: Lin9 seems to be the central structural component of MuvB complexes.
source: Since Lin9 binds to several MuvB complex proteins (Schmit et al., 2007; Wiseman et al., 2015), it seems to be the central structural component of MuvB complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from Lin9's binding to multiple MuvB proteins.

claim: Rbbp4 can bind to histones and is involved in chromatin remodeling while being a component of other complexes like NuRD.
source: Rbbp4 can bind to histones and is involved in chromatin remodeling while being a component of other complexes like NuRD (Tong et al., 1995; Zhang et al., 1998), however, its exact function as part of MuvB complexes still has to be evaluated.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tong et al., 1995; Zhang et al., 1998.

claim: During progression through the cell cycle, p130/p107, E2f4/5, and Dp dissociate from MuvB.
source: During progression through the cell cycle, p130/p107, E2f4/5, and Dp dissociate from MuvB.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell cycle-dependent complex dynamics.

claim: The MuvB core complex interacts with B-myb and Foxm1 and switches its function from a transcriptional repressor to an activator.
source: The MuvB core complex then interacts with B-myb and Foxm1 and switches its function from a transcriptional repressor to an activator (Litovchick et al., 2007; Schmit et al., 2007; Sadasivam et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing MuvB complex dynamics.

claim: The B-myb-MuvB (MMB) complex forms in S phase.
source: The B-myb-MuvB (MMB) complex forms in S phase, and is required for initial transcriptional activation and for recruiting Foxm1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MMB complex formation timing.

claim: The B-myb-MuvB complex is required for initial transcriptional activation and for recruiting Foxm1.
source: The B-myb-MuvB (MMB) complex forms in S phase, and is required for initial transcriptional activation and for recruiting Foxm1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MMB complex function.

claim: The Foxm1-MuvB complex stimulates maximum expression of G2/M cell cycle genes.
source: Finally, the Foxm1-MuvB complex stimulates maximum expression of G2/M cell cycle genes (Sadasivam et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Down et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sadasivam et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Down et al., 2012.

claim: Mutation or reduced expression of Foxm1 or B-myb lead to decreased expression levels of G2/M genes followed by defects and cellular arrest during mitosis and cytokinesis.
source: Mutation or reduced expression of Foxm1 or B-myb lead to decreased expression levels of G2/M genes followed by defects and cellular arrest during mitotis and cytokinesis (Tarasov et al., 2008; Laoukili et al., 2005; Knight et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tarasov et al., 2008; Laoukili et al., 2005; Knight et al., 2009.

claim: Depletion of Lin9, Lin52, or Lin54 leads to elevated cell cycle gene expression in G0/G1.
source: Since they are components of the transcriptional repressor and activator complexes, depletion of Lin9, Lin52, or Lin54 leads to elevated cell cycle gene expression in G0/G1 (Litovchick et al., 2007), but also to reduced expression during S, G2, and M followed by mitotic arrest (Schmit et al., 2007; Knight et al., 2009; Boichuk et al., 2013; Kittler et al., 2007; Reichert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Litovchick et al., 2007.

claim: Depletion of Lin9, Lin52, or Lin54 leads to reduced expression during S, G2, and M followed by mitotic arrest.
source: Since they are components of the transcriptional repressor and activator complexes, depletion of Lin9, Lin52, or Lin54 leads to elevated cell cycle gene expression in G0/G1 (Litovchick et al., 2007), but also to reduced expression during S, G2, and M followed by mitotic arrest (Schmit et al., 2007; Knight et al., 2009; Boichuk et al., 2013; Kittler et al., 2007; Reichert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schmit et al., 2007; Knight et al., 2009; Boichuk et al., 2013; Kittler et al., 2007; Reichert et al., 2010.

claim: Lin37 is the only MuvB component without a defined role in transcription or generally in cell cycle regulation.
source: Lin37 is the only MuvB component without a defined role in transcription or generally in cell cycle regulation.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge motivating the study.

claim: Lin37−/− cells proliferate normally.
source: We find that Lin37−/− cells proliferate normally.
evidence: This is supported by MTT assays (Figure 2B) and cell cycle analysis.

claim: DREAM no longer acts as a transcriptional repressor in G0/G1 in Lin37−/− cells.
source: However, DREAM no longer acts as a transcriptional repressor in G0/G1.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR (Figure 3B), luciferase assays (Figure 4), and RNA-seq data (Figure 6).

claim: Activation of transcription by MMB and Foxm1-MuvB complexes still functions in Lin37-deficient cells.
source: In contrast, activation of transcription by MMB and Foxm1-MuvB complexes still functions in Lin37-deficient cells.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data showing normal expression in proliferating cells (Figure 2C).

claim: DREAM without Lin37 can still assemble and bind to promoters.
source: Interestingly, DREAM without Lin37 can still assemble and bind to promoters.
evidence: This is supported by DNA pulldown assays (Figure 7A) and ChIP experiments (Figure 7B).

claim: Recruitment of p130 or p107 pocket proteins is not sufficient for cell cycle gene repression.
source: Hence, recruitment of p130 or p107 pocket proteins is not sufficient for cell cycle gene repression.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that DREAM loses repression function without Lin37 even though p130/p107 still bind to promoters.

claim: Lin37 does not contain any conserved domains with known function.
source: The sequence analysis revealed that Lin37 does not contain any conserved domains with known function.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Lin37 is highly conserved in mammals, but poorly conserved in deuterostomes.
source: Lin37 is highly conserved in mammals, but poorly conserved in deuterostomes.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Three small conserved regions in the central part of Lin37 could be identified: a potential nuclear localization signal (NLS) and two adjacent conserved domains (CD1 and CD2).
source: However, three small conserved regions in the central part of the protein could be identified: a potential nuclear localization signal (NLS) and two adjacent conserved domains (CD1 and CD2) that are separated by a spacer of eight weakly conserved amino acids.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Mutation of CD1 or CD2 leads to reduced binding to Lin9, Lin54 and B-myb.
source: Indeed, mutation of CD1 or CD2 leads to reduced binding to Lin9, Lin54 and B-myb (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Binding of Lin37 to MuvB proteins was essentially lost when both CD1 and CD2 domains were mutated simultaneously.
source: Binding was essentially lost when both domains were mutated simultaneously, providing evidence that both domains mediate binding of Lin37 to the MuvB core complex.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 1B and C).

claim: Both CD1 and CD2 domains mediate binding of Lin37 to the MuvB core complex.
source: Binding was essentially lost when both domains were mutated simultaneously, providing evidence that both domains mediate binding of Lin37 to the MuvB core complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutation of both domains abolishes binding.

claim: GFP-tagged Lin37 was clearly localized to the nucleus.
source: GFP-tagged Lin37 was clearly localized to the nucleus, while mutation of the NLS resulted in a homogeneous protein distribution in the cell.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy (Figure 1D).

claim: Mutation of the NLS resulted in a homogeneous protein distribution in the cell.
source: GFP-tagged Lin37 was clearly localized to the nucleus, while mutation of the NLS resulted in a homogeneous protein distribution in the cell.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy (Figure 1D).

claim: Mutation of CD1 and CD2 domains did not influence subcellular localization of Lin37.
source: In contrast, mutation of CD1 and CD2 domains did not influence subcellular localization (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy (Figure 1D).

claim: Proper nuclear import of Lin37 depends on the NLS, but not on the interaction with MuvB.
source: Thus, proper nuclear import of Lin37 depends on the NLS, but not on the interaction with MuvB.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization experiments showing NLS mutation affects localization but CD1/CD2 mutations do not.

claim: Both targeting approaches (exon 4 and exon 6) led to ablation of Lin37 with a high frequency of 40–60%.
source: Both targeting approaches led to ablation of Lin37 with a high frequency of 40–60% (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) showing that Lin37 is not essential for survival of these cells.
evidence: This is based on Western blot analysis of CRISPR/Cas9 treated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: Lin37 is not essential for survival of NIH3T3 cells.
source: Both targeting approaches led to ablation of Lin37 with a high frequency of 40–60% (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) showing that Lin37 is not essential for survival of these cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the ability to generate Lin37 knockout cells at high frequency.

claim: Viability of NIH3T3 cells does not depend on the expression of wild-type Lin37.
source: The results indicate that viability of the cell lines does not depend on the expression of wild-type Lin37 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by MTT assays (Figure 2B).

claim: Expression of E2f2, Mcm5, Bub1, and Nek2 was essentially unaffected by Lin37 in proliferating cells.
source: Expression of E2f2 and Mcm5, which display peak expression during S phase, and Bub1 and Nek2, which are mainly expressed during G2/M, were essentially unaffected by Lin37 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data (Figure 2C).

claim: Loss of Lin37 does not interfere with the proliferation rate or gene activation by B-myb-MuvB/Foxm1-MuvB complexes.
source: Thus, the data suggest that loss of Lin37 does not interfere with the proliferation rate or gene activation by B-myb-MuvB/Foxm1-MuvB complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the normal proliferation and gene expression in proliferating Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: Lin37 knockout cell lines maintain the potential to arrest in G0.
source: Lin37 knockout cell lines maintain the potential to arrest in G0, although a minor increase in the fraction of S and G2/M phase cells was observed.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 3A).

claim: A minor increase in the fraction of S and G2/M phase cells was observed in serum-starved Lin37 knockout cells.
source: Lin37 knockout cell lines maintain the potential to arrest in G0, although a minor increase in the fraction of S and G2/M phase cells was observed.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 3A).

claim: The number of cells in S and G2/M phases was slightly elevated at the 18 hr time point in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: Furthermore, the number of cells in S and G2/M phases was slightly elevated at the 18 hr time point (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 3A).

claim: mRNA expression analysis of early and late cell cycle genes revealed a significant de-repression in G0 and G1 in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: mRNA expression analysis of early and late cell cycle genes revealed a significant de-repression in G0 and G1.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data (Figure 3B).

claim: In S and G2/M phases, expression of both early and late cell cycle genes was still moderately elevated when Lin37 was absent or mutated.
source: In S and G2/M phases, expression of both gene groups was still moderately elevated when Lin37 was absent or mutated (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data (Figure 3B).

claim: Lin37 is required for transcriptional repression by DREAM but not for activation by B-myb-MuvB and Foxm1-MuvB.
source: These results show that Lin37 is required for transcriptional repression by DREAM but not for activation by B-myb-MuvB and Foxm1-MuvB, which is intriguing because Lin37 is a component of both the repressive and activating complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects on gene expression in G0/G1 versus S/G2/M phases.

claim: In serum-starved NIH3T3 wild-type cells, activity of DREAM target promoters was up-regulated when the E2F binding sites or the CHRs were mutated.
source: In serum-starved NIH3T3 wild-type cells, activity of DREAM target promoters was up-regulated when the E2F binding sites (Orc1, Cdc45) or the CHRs (Ttk, Ccnb2) were mutated (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4).

claim: Mutating the CHR in the Ttk promoter led to an increase in activity of merely 2-fold in knockout cells compared to 136-fold in Lin37 wild-type cells.
source: Notably, mutating the CHR in the Ttk promoter led to an increase in activity of merely 2-fold in knockout cells compared to 136-fold in Lin37 wild-type cells.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4).

claim: The Ccnb2 CHR mutant promoter displayed even slightly less activity than the wild-type promoter in Lin37−/− cells.
source: Furthermore, the Ccnb2 CHR mutant promoter displayed even slightly less activity than the wild-type promoter in Lin37−/− cells.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4).

claim: Activities of Cdc45 wild-type and E2F-site mutant promoters were not significantly different in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: Activities of Cdc45 wild-type and E2F-site mutant promoters were not significantly different in Lin37 knockout cells, while mutating the E2F binding site in the Orc1 promoter still increased activity 2.7-fold in the absence of Lin37.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4).

claim: Mutating the E2F binding site in the Orc1 promoter still increased activity 2.7-fold in the absence of Lin37.
source: Activities of Cdc45 wild-type and E2F-site mutant promoters were not significantly different in Lin37 knockout cells, while mutating the E2F binding site in the Orc1 promoter still increased activity 2.7-fold in the absence of Lin37.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4).

claim: Repression of all wild-type promoters could completely be restored when a Lin37 expression plasmid was co-transfected.
source: Importantly, repression of all wild-type promoters could completely be restored when a Lin37 expression plasmid was co-transfected (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4).

claim: Activity of DREAM is completely lost in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: As mutation of CHR sites, which exclusively bind DREAM but not E2F/Rb in repressed promoters, did not significantly increase gene expression in Lin37 knockout cells, we conclude that activity of DREAM is completely lost in these cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the luciferase reporter assay results showing no difference between wild-type and CHR mutant promoters in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: The small but significant increase of Orc1 activity upon E2F site mutation relates to E2f/Rb repressor complexes that bind to E2F elements and are still active in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: We propose that the small but significant increase of Orc1 activity upon E2F site mutation relates to E2f/Rb repressor complexes that bind to E2F elements and are still active in Lin37 knockout cells.
evidence: This is a proposed explanation for the observed data.

claim: DREAM is essential for repression of cell cycle genes through CHR and E2F sites in quiescence.
source: Together, these results strongly suggest that DREAM is essential for repression of cell cycle genes through CHR and E2F sites in quiescence and that loss of DREAM activity is not compensated by other repressor complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the complete loss of repression at CHR sites in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: Loss of DREAM activity is not compensated by other repressor complexes.
source: Together, these results strongly suggest that DREAM is essential for repression of cell cycle genes through CHR and E2F sites in quiescence and that loss of DREAM activity is not compensated by other repressor complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the complete de-repression of cell cycle genes in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: mRNA levels of G2/M and G1/S cell cycle genes were clearly increased during G0 and early G1 in cell lines expressing luciferase and the Lin37 mutant compared to cells expressing wild-type Lin37.
source: mRNA levels of G2/M (Bub1, Nek2) and G1/S (E2f2, Mcm5) cell cycle genes were clearly increased during G0 and early G1 in cell lines expressing luciferase and the Lin37 mutant compared to cells expressing wild-type Lin37.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR time course data (Figure 5A).

claim: The increase in mRNA expression was not or only to a minor extent detected in late cell cycle phases in Lin37 mutant cells.
source: In contrast, this increase in mRNA expression was not or only to a minor extent detected in late cell cycle phases, leading to a reduced maximum fold-change of all genes measured (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR time course data (Figure 5A).

claim: Downregulation of mRNA expression in G0 and early G1 can be rescued by re-expression of wild-type Lin37 but not by MuvB binding-deficient mutant Lin37.
source: Thus, downregulation of mRNA expression in G0 and early G1 can be rescued by re-expression of wild-type Lin37 but not by MuvB binding-deficient mutant Lin37.
evidence: This is inferred from the qPCR time course data (Figure 5A).

claim: Lin37 lacking a functional NLS retained its ability to fully restore DREAM function.
source: Lin37 lacking a functional NLS retained its ability to fully restore DREAM function (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 5B).

claim: CD1 and CD2 mutants could rescue DREAM function, but less efficiently than wild-type Lin37.
source: CD1 and CD2 mutants could rescue DREAM function, but less efficiently than wild-type Lin37, which is consistent with their reduced affinity for theMuvB complex (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 5B).

claim: The CD1+2 double mutant does not interact at all with the MuvB core.
source: In contrast, the CD1+2 double mutant does not interact at all with the MuvB core and was unable to restore repression of the Ttk promoter (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation (Figure 1B and C) and luciferase reporter assays (Figure 5B).

claim: The CD1+2 double mutant was unable to restore repression of the Ttk promoter.
source: In contrast, the CD1+2 double mutant does not interact at all with the MuvB core and was unable to restore repression of the Ttk promoter (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 5B).

claim: Binding of Lin37 to DREAM is essential for repression of cell cycle genes.
source: Taken together, our results provide evidence that binding of Lin37 to DREAM is essential for repression of cell cycle genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing only wild-type Lin37 can restore repression.

claim: Over-expression of cyclin D1 leads to a reduced volume of proliferating and contact inhibited NIH3T3 cells.
source: It has been shown that over-expression of cyclin D1 leads to a reduced volume of proliferating and contact inhibited NIH3T3 cells (Quelle et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Quelle et al., 1993.

claim: Lin37 knockouts and cells expressing the MuvB-binding deficient mutant appear to be slightly larger than cells expressing wild-type Lin37.
source: However, we found that Lin37 knockouts and cells expressing the MuvB-binding deficient mutant appear to be slightly larger than cells expressing wild-type Lin37 (Figure 5C), but these changes in the cell volume were not significant.
evidence: This is supported by Coulter counter analysis (Figure 5C).

claim: Changes in the cell volume in Lin37 knockout cells were not significant.
source: However, we found that Lin37 knockouts and cells expressing the MuvB-binding deficient mutant appear to be slightly larger than cells expressing wild-type Lin37 (Figure 5C), but these changes in the cell volume were not significant.
evidence: This is supported by Coulter counter analysis (Figure 5C).

claim: Loss of Lin37 does not reduce the cell volume as over-expression of cyclin D1 does.
source: Thus, loss of Lin37 does not reduce the cell volume as over-expression of cyclin D1 does.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell volume measurements.

claim: 387 genes were significantly up-regulated in serum-starved Lin37−/− cells compared to cells expressing wild-type Lin37.
source: One technical and two biological replicates were performed, which led to the identification of 387 significantly up- and 76 significantly down-regulated genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 76 genes were significantly down-regulated in serum-starved Lin37−/− cells compared to cells expressing wild-type Lin37.
source: One technical and two biological replicates were performed, which led to the identification of 387 significantly up- and 76 significantly down-regulated genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Gene Ontology analysis showed a highly significant enrichment of cell cycle-related processes for the up-regulated genes.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis showed a highly significant enrichment of cell cycle-related processes for the up-regulated genes (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 2), including processes connected to S phase (e.g. DNA replication, DNA metabolic process) and to mitosis (e.g. chromosome segregation, mitotic nuclear division).
evidence: This is based on GO analysis of RNA-seq data (Figure 6A).

claim: 77.5% of the top 40 de-repressed protein-coding genes have been identified as DREAM targets by ChIP-chip.
source: 77.5% of the top 40 de-repressed protein-coding genes (Figure 6B) have been identified as DREAM targets by ChIP-chip (Litovchick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq data with published ChIP-chip data.

claim: 65% of the top hits are cell cycle genes with an expression maximum in G2 and mitosis and contain evolutionary conserved CHR promoter elements close to their transcription start sites.
source: 65% of the top hits are cell cycle genes with an expression maximum in G2 and mitosis and contain evolutionary conserved CHR promoter elements close to their transcription start sites.
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA-seq data and comparison with known cell cycle genes.

claim: Expression of more than one third of cell cycle genes de-repressed in Lin37−/− cells displayed peak expression in S phase.
source: Additionally, expression of more than one third of cell cycle genes de-repressed in Lin37−/− cells displayed peak expression in S phase (Figure 6C) and can bind DREAM though E2F sites (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA-seq data (Figure 6C).

claim: Both G2/M and G1/S cell cycle genes were affected by loss of Lin37.
source: Thus, both G2/M and G1/S cell cycle genes were affected by loss of Lin37.
evidence: This is inferred from the RNA-seq analysis showing de-repression of both gene classes.

claim: Expression of four of the MuvB complex components – Foxm1, B-myb (Mybl2), Lin9, and Lin54 – were also up-regulated in Lin37 knockout cells.
source: Interestingly, expression of four of the MuvB complex components – Foxm1, B-myb (Mybl2), Lin9, and Lin54 – were also up-regulated in Lin37 knockout cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data (Figure 6B).

claim: 157 Lin37-regulated genes are bound by DREAM and differentially expressed in the cell cycle.
source: Furthermore, analysis of all Lin37-regulated genes revealed that 157 of their human orthologues are bound by DREAM and differentially expressed in the cell cycle, while 42 and 43 are identified exclusively as DREAM targets or cell cycle genes, respectively.
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq data with published datasets (Figure 6D).

claim: 42 Lin37-regulated genes are identified exclusively as DREAM targets.
source: Furthermore, analysis of all Lin37-regulated genes revealed that 157 of their human orthologues are bound by DREAM and differentially expressed in the cell cycle, while 42 and 43 are identified exclusively as DREAM targets or cell cycle genes, respectively.
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq data with published datasets (Figure 6D).

claim: 43 Lin37-regulated genes are identified exclusively as cell cycle genes.
source: Furthermore, analysis of all Lin37-regulated genes revealed that 157 of their human orthologues are bound by DREAM and differentially expressed in the cell cycle, while 42 and 43 are identified exclusively as DREAM targets or cell cycle genes, respectively.
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq data with published datasets (Figure 6D).

claim: 60 of the 115 Lin37 targets without experimentally validated cell cycle expression have been predicted to be cell cycle genes.
source: However, 60 of the 115 Lin37 targets without experimentally validated cell cycle expression have been predicted to be cell cycle genes (www.targetgenereg.org) (Fischer et al., 2016), suggesting that the actual overlap between Lin37 targets and cell cycle genes may be larger.
evidence: This is based on comparison with predicted cell cycle genes from targetgenereg.org.

claim: None of the down-regulated genes bind DREAM.
source: In contrast to the genes up-regulated in Lin37−/− cells, none of the down-regulated genes bind DREAM and only four were identified as cell cycle genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq data with DREAM binding data.

claim: Only four of the down-regulated genes were identified as cell cycle genes.
source: In contrast to the genes up-regulated in Lin37−/− cells, none of the down-regulated genes bind DREAM and only four were identified as cell cycle genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq data with cell cycle gene datasets.

claim: DREAM targets and cell cycle genes are generally up-regulated when Lin37 is not expressed.
source: Together, the transcriptome-wide analysis reveals that DREAM targets and cell cycle genes are generally up-regulated when Lin37 is not expressed.
evidence: This is inferred from the RNA-seq analysis showing enrichment of DREAM targets and cell cycle genes among up-regulated genes.

claim: DREAM components were purified from both wild-type and from Lin37 knockout nuclear extracts using DNA pulldown assays.
source: DREAM-specific proteins were purified from both wild-type and from Lin37 knockout nuclear extracts (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by DNA pulldown experiments (Figure 7A).

claim: DREAM can assemble at CHR sites of DNA probes in vitro even in the absence of Lin37.
source: These findings show that DREAM can assemble at CHR sites of DNA probes in vitro even in the absence of Lin37.
evidence: This is inferred from the DNA pulldown experiments showing DREAM components bind to CHR-containing DNA in Lin37 knockout extracts.

claim: Binding signals of Lin37 at G1/S and G2/M cell cycle gene promoters were dramatically decreased in Lin37−/− cells.
source: Binding signals of Lin37 at G1/S and G2/M cell cycle gene promoters were dramatically decreased in Lin37−/− cells, and binding of the DREAM components Lin54, E2f4, and p130 was only slightly or not altered (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR experiments (Figure 7B).

claim: Binding of the DREAM components Lin54, E2f4, and p130 was only slightly or not altered in Lin37−/− cells.
source: Binding signals of Lin37 at G1/S and G2/M cell cycle gene promoters were dramatically decreased in Lin37−/− cells, and binding of the DREAM components Lin54, E2f4, and p130 was only slightly or not altered (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR experiments (Figure 7B).

claim: DREAM components assemble, but form a non-functional complex when Lin37 is absent.
source: The results obtained with both experimental approaches show that DREAM components assemble, but form a non-functional complex when Lin37 is absent.
evidence: This is inferred from the DNA pulldown and ChIP experiments showing DREAM binds to promoters but does not repress genes without Lin37.

claim: Five Lin37-deficient C2C12 single cell clones were selected for analysis.
source: Five Lin37-deficient single cell clones were selected for further analysis and compared with the C2C12 parental cell line and 4 clones that were treated with CRISPR/Cas9-nickase constructs but remained wild-type for Lin37 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The percentages of cells in G1, S, and G2/M phases of the cell cycle did not significantly change in proliferating or serum-starved Lin37-deficient C2C12 cells.
source: Flow cytometry revealed that the percentages of cells in G1, S, and G2/M phases of the cell cycle did not significantly change either in proliferating or in serum-starved cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry analysis (Figure 8B).

claim: Lin37-deficient C2C12 cells proliferate normally and can arrest under growth limiting conditions.
source: Thus, Lin37-deficient C2C12 cells proliferate normally and can arrest under growth limiting conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell cycle analysis showing normal distribution in proliferating and arrested cells.

claim: Knockout of Lin37 led to a loss of DREAM function in quiescent C2C12 cells.
source: However, as observed in fibroblasts, knockout of Lin37 lead to a loss of DREAM function in quiescent C2C12 cells.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis (Figure 8C) and luciferase assays (Figure 8D).

claim: Expression of early and late cell cycle genes remained basically unchanged between proliferating wild-type and knockout C2C12 cells.
source: While the expression of early and late cell cycle genes remained basically unchanged between proliferating wild-type and knockout cells, expression was highly increased in serum-starved knockout cells (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis (Figure 8C).

claim: Expression of early and late cell cycle genes was highly increased in serum-starved Lin37 knockout C2C12 cells.
source: While the expression of early and late cell cycle genes remained basically unchanged between proliferating wild-type and knockout cells, expression was highly increased in serum-starved knockout cells (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis (Figure 8C).

claim: Re-expression of Lin37 completely rescued DREAM function in all C2C12 cell clones.
source: However, re-expression of Lin37 completely rescued DREAM function in all cell clones.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 8D).

claim: The data from C2C12 myoblast cells reflect the results obtained with NIH3T3 cells.
source: Taken together, the data from C2C12 myoblast cells reflect the results obtained with NIH3T3 cells, which suggests that the Lin37 knockout phenotype is a general phenomenon.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar phenotypes observed in both cell types.

claim: The Lin37 knockout phenotype is a general phenomenon.
source: Taken together, the data from C2C12 myoblast cells reflect the results obtained with NIH3T3 cells, which suggests that the Lin37 knockout phenotype is a general phenomenon.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of similar phenotypes in two different cell types.

claim: Triple knockout of all pocket proteins leads to an inability of cells to enter quiescence in response to serum deprivation and contact inhibition.
source: It has been shown that triple knockout of all pocket proteins leads to an inability of cells to enter quiescence in response to serum deprivation and contact inhibition (Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000; Classon et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dannenberg et al., 2000; Sage et al., 2000; Classon et al., 2000.

claim: Rb single knockout cells proliferated normally.
source: Similar to Lin37 knockouts, Rb single knockout cells proliferated normally.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9B).

claim: Proliferating Lin37/Rb double-negative cells exhibited a significant decrease of cells in G1 accompanied by an increase of S and G2/M populations.
source: In contrast, proliferating double-negative cells exhibited a significant decrease of cells in G1 accompanied by an increase of S and G2/M populations (Figure 9B), suggesting a reduced length of the G1 phase.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9B).

claim: Cells depleted of either Lin37 or Rb arrested in G0.
source: Using both serum deprivation and density growth inhibition, we found that cells depleted of either Lin37 or Rb arrested in G0.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9B).

claim: Lin37/Rb double knockout cells displayed a highly significant decrease of G0/G1 cells and an increase of S and G2/M phase cells indicative for the loss of the restriction point.
source: In contrast, Lin37/Rb double knockout (DKO) cells displayed a highly significant decrease of G0/G1 cells and an increase of S and G2/M phase cells indicative for the loss of the restriction point (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9B).

claim: Loss of Lin37 led to a significant up-regulation of cell cycle gene expression in density-arrested and serum-starved cells.
source: Loss of Lin37 led to a significant up-regulation of gene expression in density-arrested and serum-starved cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis (Figure 9C).

claim: A less pronounced de-repression was detected in Rb-negative cells.
source: A less pronounced de-repression was detected in Rb-negative cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis (Figure 9C).

claim: Cell cycle gene expression in Lin37−/−/Rb−/− cell clones was most significantly up-regulated and generally unchanged between proliferating and density-arrested or serum-starved cells.
source: Cell cycle gene expression in Lin37−/−/Rb−/− cell clones, however, was most significantly up-regulated and generally unchanged between proliferating and density-arrested or serum-starved cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis (Figure 9C).

claim: Expression of Bub1 and Mcm5 was elevated during G0 and G1 in all mutant cell lines.
source: In all mutant cell lines, expression of the G2/M cell cycle gene Bub1 and the G1/S cell cycle gene Mcm5 was elevated during G0 and G1.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR time course data (Figure 9D).

claim: Expression was almost at its maximum in Lin37/Rb double knockout cells immediately after the serum deprivation period.
source: Expression was almost at its maximum in DKO cells immediately after the serum deprivation period, and the Lin37-/- and Rb-/- single knockout lines exhibited an intermediate phenotype with a more pronounced de-repression in the Lin37−/− cells.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR time course data (Figure 9D).

claim: Lin37−/−/Rb−/− cells largely lose their potential to respond to serum starvation and re-stimulation.
source: These observations are consistent with the DNA content of the cells at the given time points, showing that Lin37−/−/Rb−/− cells largely lose their potential to respond to serum starvation and re-stimulation (Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9—source data 1).

claim: Wild-type and single knockout cells displayed a clear enrichment of 2 n cells after the serum starvation period followed by accumulation of S phase and G2/M cells upon re-stimulation.
source: In contrast, wild-type and single knockout cells displayed a clear enrichment of 2 n cells after the serum starvation period followed by accumulation of S phase and G2/M cells upon re-stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis (Figure 9—source data 1).

claim: In serum-starved Rb−/− cells, Cdc45 and Ttk wild-type promoters were de-repressed.
source: In serum-starved Rb−/− cells, Cdc45 (maximum expression in G1/S) and Ttk (maximum expression in G2/M) wild-type promoters were de-repressed, even if the activity of the Ttk promoter was still 10-fold lower than the corresponding CHR promoter mutant (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 10A).

claim: Repression of Cdc45 and Ttk promoters could be rescued by expression of wild-type Rb, but not by a mutant that is unable to bind E2f proteins (Rb del22).
source: Repression of both promoters could be rescued by expression of wild-type Rb, but not by a mutant that is unable to bind E2f proteins (Rb del22).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 10A).

claim: In Lin37/Rb double knockout cells, both Cdc45 and Ttk promoters were completely de-repressed in quiescence.
source: In Lin37/Rb double knockout cells, both promoters were completely de-repressed in quiescence (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 10B).

claim: Expression of Lin37 or Rb could only partially rescue repression in Lin37/Rb double knockout cells.
source: Expression of Lin37 or Rb could only partially rescue repression with a more pronounced effect of Rb on the Cdc45 promoter that binds DREAM and Rb and of Lin37 on the Ttk promoter that binds only DREAM.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 10B).

claim: Combined expression of both Lin37 and Rb completely rescued promoter repression after serum deprivation.
source: Combined expression of both proteins completely rescued promoter repression after serum deprivation.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 10B).

claim: Both Lin37 and Rb are necessary for proper cell cycle gene regulation.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that both Lin37 and Rb are necessary for proper cell cycle gene regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing both are needed for full repression.

claim: Combined loss of Lin37 and Rb leads to de-regulation of cell cycle genes and an inability of cells to respond with cell cycle arrest to growth-inhibiting conditions.
source: Their combined loss leads to de-regulation of cell cycle genes and an inability of cells to respond with cell cycle arrest to growth-inhibiting conditions.
evidence: This is supported by the cell cycle and gene expression data in double knockout cells.

claim: The mechanism beyond the key function of Lin37 in transcriptional repression by DREAM is still unclear.
source: However, the mechanism beyond the key function of Lin37 in transcriptional repression by DREAM is still unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current study.

claim: p130 and p107 can recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes.
source: The pocket proteins p130/p107 can recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes (Classon and Dyson, 2001) which may support a compact nucleosome structure leading to gene repression.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Classon and Dyson, 2001.

claim: Combined knockdown of both p130 and p107 leads to a loss of DREAM function.
source: Combined knockdown of both proteins leads to a loss of DREAM function (Litovchick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Litovchick et al., 2007.

claim: p130/p107 cannot repress cell cycle genes when Lin37 is absent or unable to bind to DREAM, although they are still recruited to target gene promoters.
source: However, our results provide evidence that p130/p107 cannot repress cell cycle genes when Lin37 is absent or unable to bind to DREAM, although they are still recruited to target gene promoters (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP and DNA pulldown experiments (Figure 7).

claim: Lin37 may recruit yet unknown proteins that are essential for repression by DREAM – most likely chromatin modifiers.
source: First, Lin37 may recruit yet unknown proteins that are essential for repression by DREAM – most likely chromatin modifiers.
evidence: This is proposed as a possible explanation for Lin37's function.

claim: Loss of Lin37 binding may render DREAM inactive because of conformational changes.
source: Second, loss of Lin37 binding may render DREAM inactive because of conformational changes, which may prevent proper positioning of the complex or inhibit binding of proteins to DREAM without directly contacting Lin37.
evidence: This is proposed as a possible explanation for Lin37's function.

claim: Loss of Lin37 could change post-translational modifications at other DREAM components that are necessary for function of the complex.
source: Third, loss of Lin37 could change post-translational modifications at other DREAM components, possibly p130/p107, that are necessary for function of the complex.
evidence: This is proposed as a possible explanation for Lin37's function.

claim: Knockdown of DREAM components led to only a moderate or no de-repression of cell cycle gene expression in serum-starved cells.
source: Given that knockdown of DREAM components led to only a moderate (Litovchick et al., 2007) or no (Schmit et al., 2007) de-repression of cell cycle gene expression in serum-starved cells, it was suggested that DREAM may act redundantly with other repressor complexes like NuRD to repress genes in quiescence.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Litovchick et al., 2007 and Schmit et al., 2007.

claim: The results provide strong evidence that DREAM is an essential transcriptional repressor to induce quiescence.
source: In contrast, the results presented here provide strong evidence that DREAM is an essential transcriptional repressor to induce quiescence.
evidence: This is inferred from the complete loss of repression in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: In quiescent cells, loss of DREAM function cannot be compensated by E2f/Rb or by chromatin-modifying complexes.
source: Hence, in quiescent cells, loss of DREAM function cannot be compensated by E2f/Rb or by chromatin-modifying complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the complete de-repression of cell cycle genes in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: It is unlikely that other proteins binding to CHR sites independent of DREAM contribute to repression.
source: Thus, it is unlikely that other proteins binding to CHR sites independent of DREAM contribute to repression.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CHR mutant promoters are not more active than wild-type promoters in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: Either DREAM or E2f/Rb is sufficient to induce G0/G1 arrest.
source: These results indicate that either DREAM or E2f/Rb is sufficient to induce G0/G1 arrest, even if many cell cycle genes are de-repressed when only one of both complexes is disturbed.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that single knockouts can still arrest but double knockouts cannot.

claim: Rb and p130/p107 may regulate gene expression through different mechanisms.
source: In general, our data in combination with earlier findings suggest that Rb and p130/p107 may regulate gene expression through different mechanisms.
evidence: This is inferred from the different binding specificities and complex compositions.

claim: Rb can recruit a large variety of chromatin-modifying enzymes through its LxCxE binding cleft.
source: While Rb can recruit a large variety of chromatin-modifying enzymes through its LxCxE binding cleft, this domain in p130/p107 is essential for DREAM formation and binds to Lin52 (Guiley et al., 2015) making it inaccessible for other proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rb function.

claim: The LxCxE binding domain in p130/p107 is essential for DREAM formation and binds to Lin52.
source: While Rb can recruit a large variety of chromatin-modifying enzymes through its LxCxE binding cleft, this domain in p130/p107 is essential for DREAM formation and binds to Lin52 (Guiley et al., 2015) making it inaccessible for other proteins.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guiley et al., 2015.

claim: Binding of Rb to E2f/Dp complexes is sufficient for repressing target genes.
source: Furthermore, binding of Rb to E2f/Dp complexes is sufficient for repressing target genes, while p130/p107 function depends also on MuvB proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing p130/p107 cannot repress without Lin37.

claim: p130/p107 function depends also on MuvB proteins.
source: Furthermore, binding of Rb to E2f/Dp complexes is sufficient for repressing target genes, while p130/p107 function depends also on MuvB proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing p130/p107 cannot repress without Lin37.

claim: Lin37 may be a tumor suppressor.
source: The strong activation of cell cycle gene expression in serum-starved Lin37−/− cells as well as the inability of cells to enter quiescence when both Lin37 and Rb are depleted (Figure 9, Figure 9—source data 1) indicate that Lin37 may be a tumor suppressor.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypes observed in Lin37 knockout cells.

claim: Expression of E2f1, E2f2, Mybl2/B-myb, and Foxm1 is up-regulated in Lin37−/− cells.
source: Furthermore, expression of the transcriptional activators E2f1, E2f2, Mybl2/B-myb, and Foxm1 is up-regulated in Lin37−/− cells (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data (Figure 6).

claim: E2f1, E2f2, Mybl2/B-myb, and Foxm1 are highly expressed in many cancer types which generally predicts poor patient prognosis.
source: These genes are highly expressed in many cancer types which generally predicts poor patient prognosis (Gentles et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gentles et al., 2015.

claim: Viral proteins like HPV E7 and SV40 large T antigen support transformation of cells and cancer development.
source: Moreover, viral proteins like HPV E7 and SV40 large T antigen support transformation of cells and cancer development (McLaughlin-Drubin and Münger, 2009) and disrupt DREAM (Fischer et al., 2017; Nor Rashid et al., 2011; Pang et al., 2014) as well as E2f/Rb complexes (Dyson et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: HPV E7 and SV40 large T antigen disrupt DREAM.
source: Moreover, viral proteins like HPV E7 and SV40 large T antigen support transformation of cells and cancer development (McLaughlin-Drubin and Münger, 2009) and disrupt DREAM (Fischer et al., 2017; Nor Rashid et al., 2011; Pang et al., 2014) as well as E2f/Rb complexes (Dyson et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fischer et al., 2017; Nor Rashid et al., 2011; Pang et al., 2014.

claim: HPV E7 and SV40 large T antigen disrupt E2f/Rb complexes.
source: Moreover, viral proteins like HPV E7 and SV40 large T antigen support transformation of cells and cancer development (McLaughlin-Drubin and Münger, 2009) and disrupt DREAM (Fischer et al., 2017; Nor Rashid et al., 2011; Pang et al., 2014) as well as E2f/Rb complexes (Dyson et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dyson et al., 1989.

claim: Mutations of p130 or p107 are only rarely found in cancer.
source: In contrast to Rb, mutations of p130 or p107 are only rarely found in cancer (Cinti et al., 2000; Helin et al., 1997; Claudio et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cinti et al., 2000; Helin et al., 1997; Claudio et al., 2000.

claim: p130 and p107 have been shown to exhibit tumor suppressive functions in Rb null mouse models.
source: However, p130 and p107 have been shown to exhibit tumor suppressive functions in Rb null mouse models when loss of p130 and p107 can support tumor development (Wirt and Sage, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wirt and Sage, 2010.

claim: Lin37 may be inactivated only in specific types of cancer or be alternatively mutated to p130 or p107.
source: Considering that p130/p107 and Lin37 are connected through their function in transcriptional repression, Lin37 may be inactivated only in specific types of cancer or be alternatively mutated to p130 or p107.
evidence: This is speculation about potential roles of Lin37 in cancer.

claim: Lin37 is essential for cell cycle gene repression in cellular quiescence.
source: Taken together, our data reveal that Lin37 is essential for cell cycle gene repression in cellular quiescence and that a combined loss of Lin37 and Rb impairs cell cycle arrest in response to growth-limiting signals.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by multiple experiments.

claim: A combined loss of Lin37 and Rb impairs cell cycle arrest in response to growth-limiting signals.
source: Taken together, our data reveal that Lin37 is essential for cell cycle gene repression in cellular quiescence and that a combined loss of Lin37 and Rb impairs cell cycle arrest in response to growth-limiting signals.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by the double knockout experiments.

claim: Lin37 has a role in cell transformation and cancer development.
source: This indicates a role of Lin37 in cell transformation and cancer development.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypes and the role of DREAM in cell cycle control.
